views.name: orders_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  orderid,
  customerid,
  employeeid,
  orderdate,
  requireddate,
  shippeddate,
  shipvia,
  freight,
  shipname,
  shipaddress,
  shipcity,
  shipregion,
  shippostalcode,
  shipcountry
FROM orders
WHERE 1=1
views.description: One-row-per-order projection that canonicalizes key temporal and identifier columns and exposes common order attributes for joins and reporting. Use this as the normalized orders relation to join to details, customers, employees, shippers, or to aggregate by date ranges. | Use for: order-level reports (counts, freight sums) by date, customer, employee, ship country; filtering orders with/without shippeddate (shipped vs unshipped); joining to order_details for line-level analysis

views.name: order_lines
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  orderid,
  productid,
  unitprice,
  quantity,
  discount
FROM order_details
WHERE 1=1
views.description: One-row-per-order-line (order_details) projection exposing pricing and quantity measures and identifiers for joins to orders and products. | Use for: line-level revenue/quantity calculations; joining to orders/products/customers for sales analysis; discount and unitprice analyses

views.name: products_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  productid,
  productname,
  supplierid,
  categoryid,
  quantityperunit,
  unitprice,
  unitsinstock,
  unitsonorder,
  reorderlevel,
  discontinued
FROM products
WHERE 1=1
views.description: One-row-per-product projection exposing product attributes and inventory/price measures for catalogs or inventory reporting and for joining to order lines. | Use for: inventory level reports, reorder suggestions, product price lists; joining to order_details to compute sales by product or category

views.name: customers_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customerid,
  companyname,
  contactname,
  contacttitle,
  address,
  city,
  region,
  postalcode,
  country,
  phone,
  fax
FROM customers
WHERE 1=1
views.description: One-row-per-customer projection exposing identifying and address attributes for customer-level reporting and joins. | Use for: customer counts by country/city, customer contact lists, joining customers to orders

views.name: order_line_amounts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  orderid,
  productid,
  unitprice,
  quantity,
  discount,
  (unitprice * quantity) AS line_total,
  (unitprice * quantity * discount) AS line_discount_amount,
  (unitprice * quantity * (1.0 - discount)) AS line_net
FROM order_details
WHERE 1=1
views.description: Compute monetary measures for each order line: extended line total (before discount), discount amount, and net line total. Useful when aggregating sales by order/product/customer. | Use for: sales totals by order/product/customer; discount impact analysis; gross vs net revenue

views.name: orders_with_totals
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.orderid,
  o.customerid,
  o.employeeid,
  o.orderdate,
  o.requireddate,
  o.shippeddate,
  o.shipvia,
  o.freight,
  o.shipname,
  o.shipaddress,
  o.shipcity,
  o.shipregion,
  o.shippostalcode,
  o.shipcountry,
  IFNULL(SUM(od.unitprice * od.quantity), 0) AS total_before_discount,
  IFNULL(SUM(od.unitprice * od.quantity * od.discount), 0) AS total_discount_amount,
  IFNULL(SUM(od.unitprice * od.quantity * (1.0 - od.discount)), 0) AS total_net_amount,
  IFNULL(SUM(od.quantity), 0) AS total_quantity
FROM orders AS o
LEFT JOIN order_details AS od ON od.orderid = o.orderid
GROUP BY
  o.orderid,
  o.customerid,
  o.employeeid,
  o.orderdate,
  o.requireddate,
  o.shippeddate,
  o.shipvia,
  o.freight,
  o.shipname,
  o.shipaddress,
  o.shipcity,
  o.shipregion,
  o.shippostalcode,
  o.shipcountry
views.description: One-row-per-order enriched with aggregated order-level measures (sum of line totals, sum of discounts, net total, total quantity). Useful for order-level reporting and joins to customers or employees. | Use for: order revenue summaries, shipped vs unshipped revenue, per-customer order history aggregation

views.name: sales_by_product
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  od.productid,
  SUM(od.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold,
  SUM(od.unitprice * od.quantity) AS total_gross_sales,
  SUM(od.unitprice * od.quantity * od.discount) AS total_discount_amount,
  SUM(od.unitprice * od.quantity * (1.0 - od.discount)) AS total_net_sales
FROM order_details AS od
GROUP BY od.productid
views.description: Aggregated sales metrics at the product level: total quantity sold, total gross sales, total discounts, and total net sales. Use to rank products or to join to products table for attributes. | Use for: top-selling products, revenue by product, discount impact per product, join to products for category-level rollups

views.name: employees_hierarchy
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  employeeid,
  lastname,
  firstname,
  title,
  reportsto
FROM employees
WHERE 1=1
views.description: Employee self-relationship mapping preserving manager (reportsto). One row per employee with manager id exposed. Useful to build management hierarchies or to join to employees for manager names. | Use for: building org charts, resolving manager names by joining employees to itself, count reports per manager

views.name: customer_addresses
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customerid,
  companyname,
  contactname,
  address,
  city,
  region,
  postalcode,
  country,
  phone
FROM customers
WHERE 1=1
views.description: Customer contact/address subset useful for geographic cohorts (country/city). Use this to filter or join customers by location. No hard-coded location filters included so consumers can apply their own predicates. | Use for: customer cohorts by country/city, mailing lists, geospatial summaries

views.name: product_category_lookup
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.productid,
  p.productname,
  p.supplierid,
  s.companyname AS companyname,
  p.categoryid,
  c.categoryname AS categoryname,
  p.quantityperunit,
  p.unitprice,
  p.unitsinstock,
  p.unitsonorder,
  p.reorderlevel,
  p.discontinued
FROM products AS p
LEFT JOIN suppliers AS s ON s.supplierid = p.supplierid
LEFT JOIN categories AS c ON c.categoryid = p.categoryid
views.description: Denormalized product with category and supplier identifiers and names. One row per product including categoryname and supplier companyname to simplify downstream reporting and filters. | Use for: catalog listings with category and supplier names, product-level filters by supplier/category

views.name: orders_customer_employee
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.orderid,
  o.customerid,
  c.companyname AS companyname,
  c.country AS country,
  o.employeeid,
  e.firstname AS firstname,
  e.lastname AS lastname,
  o.orderdate,
  o.shippeddate,
  o.freight
FROM orders AS o
LEFT JOIN customers AS c ON c.customerid = o.customerid
LEFT JOIN employees AS e ON e.employeeid = o.employeeid
views.description: Orders enriched with customer and employee basic attributes for reporting where you want orders contextualized by buyer and sales rep. | Use for: order counts and amounts by sales rep or customer country, unshipped order follow-ups
